content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early-to-mid forecast horizon (especially 1–7 days ahead), especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in late forecast horizon (last 10–30 days), particularly when true values show mean reversion or downward momentum.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp upward spikes (e.g., 90+ → 95+), then fails to correct downward quickly.
- Shows persistent lag in capturing true price reversals — often delays turning point by 2–5 days.
- Underestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., <85) and overestimates in high-price regimes (e.g., >95).
- Mean reversion bias: forecasts too much downward drift after high peaks, too little after low troughs.
- Horizon-dependent: 1–7 day forecasts are too low, 10–30 day forecasts are too high, especially when true values show strong mean reversion.
- Avoids “overfitting to recent high” — model doesn’t adjust for recent high prices when true values are falling.
